title: KIFF audit evidence contract
description: Language-neutral shape that deterministic evidence collectors emit for an audit to consume. Python: `kiff-scan scan --format json` (the reference implementation, whose taxonomy this contract adopts). Go: `kiff scan -format json`. Other languages: any collector that conforms. The audit skill treats this as evidence, never as a verdict: a finding is an unreviewed signal, and the absence of findings is not a pass.

revision.description: Commit sha or `git describe` output. Required for a reproducible audit.

category.description: Consequence category. Canonical IDs are the kiff-scan taxonomy (src/kiff_scan/taxonomy.py), which every collector MUST emit so findings are comparable across a polyglot repository. Each carries a fixed default severity and a state_dependent flag: a state-dependent consequence is one whose safety cannot be decided from the call alone, which is exactly the class a governance runtime exists to gate.

tool.description: Model-reachable entry point that reaches the sink.

governed.description: Whether a recognized decision boundary was found on the path. Absence of a boundary is not proof of exploitability.

state_dependent.description: Whether this consequence's safety depends on live state rather than on the call alone.

coverage.description: What the collector could and could not analyze. The audit reports these as `not assessable` rather than as passes.
